title: Add token-quality signals and entropy-segmentation telemetry
author: Asha Patel
release_notes: Adds per-token quality metrics and entropy-segmentation dashboards; exposes sampling hooks for trace joiners and a default alert profile for token-degradation SLOs.
description:
Motivation: We need higher-fidelity signals for long-tail quality degradation that are orthogonal to latency/cost metrics. Current observability focuses on token counts and latency phases; it misses subtle per-token quality regressions (repetition, high-entropy hallucination bursts, truncation artifacts) that correlate with customer-facing failures. This change introduces a compact set of token-quality signals and an entropy-based segmentation layer so we can detect, alert, and debug quality regressions at scale.

What this PR does (high level):
- Introduces per-invocation token-quality metrics: token_entropy, token_repetition_score, token_alignment_score (approximate alignment to expected token distribution when reference available), and token_truncation_flag. These are aggregated into per-route and per-model rollups.
- Adds entropy-segmentation: requests are tagged into low/medium/high entropy buckets at ingest time; all downstream counters/gauges are labeled with entropy_segment to enable cohorted SLOs and alert suppression.
- Trace/log join: lightweight trace anchors are emitted when a token stream crosses a configured entropy threshold; these anchors allow the trace/ log merge pipeline to pull compact log excerpts without full trace hydration. Implemented as a 1-way sampling hook to avoid trace amplification.
- Dashboards: new "Token Quality Cohorts" dashboard with entropy distribution heatmap, repetition score CDF, top offending prompt shapes, and a per-model token-quality timeline.
- Alerts: new default alert rule token-quality-degrade (severity: P3 by default) that triggers on sustained increases in high-entropy fraction or a jump in median repetition_score. Alerts are calibrated to avoid noisy bursts with a 10m window and asymmetric decay.
- Instrumentation changes: small additions to the runtime to compute token-level entropy cheaply (approximate log-probs sketching), and a sampling-safe path that avoids extra allocations on hot code paths. All telemetry is behind the feature flag observability.token_quality=true.

Files and surface area changed (high level):
- redwood/runtime/token_metrics.cc (entropy sketch + lightweight repetition detector)
- redwood/observability/telemetry_ingest/segmenter.go (entropy segmentation and labels)
- redwood/observability/tracing/anchor_emitter.py (trace anchor helper and sample policy)
- redwood/console/dashboards/token_quality_cohorts.json (grafana-style dashboard JSON)
- redwood/console/alerts/token_quality_rules.yaml (alert rule templates and default suppression)
- redwood/sdk-python/redwood/telemetry.py (client helper to opt-in and read cohort labels)
- docs/obs/token-quality.md (design doc + runbook)
- tests/observability/test_entropy_segmentation.py (unit), tests/runtime/test_repetition_detector.cc (C++ unit)
- ci: added a lightweight loadcheck script to smoke the telemetry path in presubmit.

Commits summary: 
- commit 1: "runtime: add approximate entropy sketch and repetition detector" — core runtime changes, microbenchmarks attached.
- commit 2: "observability: entropy segmentation + ingestion labels" — ingest pipeline labeling and storage mapping changes.
- commit 3: "console: token quality cohorts dashboard + alert rules" — dashboard and alert templates.
- commit 4: "sdk/docs/tests: opt-in helpers and runbook" — SDK surface and docs.

Testing and perf: 
- Unit tests added for segmentation logic and repetition detector.
- Microbenchmarks: entropy sketch adds ~0.6% CPU on worst-case generation workloads (measured on p3-standard); memory overhead is <1MB per serving thread.
- End-to-end smoke: synthetic harness with 10k small prompts exercised the ingestion + dashboard pipeline successfully in staging.

Rollout plan: 
- Feature flag gated (observability.token_quality). Default off for existing customers.
- Phased rollout: opt-in tenants in staging -> small vendor tenant group (10 customers) for 48h -> platform-wide on by default but off for Dedicated accounts unless requested.
- Alerts default to P3 and have a 1-host cooldown; SRE will review escalations during the canary window.

Backward compatibility & migration notes: 
- No breaking runtime API changes. Segmentation labels are additive. Existing dashboards are unaffected.
- Storage mapping introduces a new label (entropy_segment) on several rollups; index size increase estimated at +3%.

Related work: ENG-4201 (token-quality sprints), ENG-4233 (entropy sketch prototype), and a linked design doc in docs/obs/token-quality.md. Also relates to ENG-3910 (alert dampening research).

Why this is different from existing token telemetry: Unlike token-cost/latency work which attributes spend, this PR focuses on per-token quality signals that enable cohorted SLOs for correctness. Entropy-segmentation lets us separate noisy/high-variance requests so alerts and dashboards are less polluted by benign bursts.

TODO in follow-ups: calibration across languages, integrating alignment_score with eval harness for automated regression detection, and exposing sampled token excerpts in the console for triage.

merge_details: Merged by Camille Laurent using squash-and-merge. PR closed 2025-10-21. Merge commit includes microbenchmarks and docs.
notes_for_oncall: If token-quality-degrade alert fires, first check entropy_segment heatmap for bursty traffic. Use trace anchors (trace_id / anchor_id in alert) to pull compact log excerpts. If noise is tenant-local, use tenant opt-out for the rule and file ENG follow-up for calibration. Run the included perf-smoke script in ci/presubmit if repro is needed.
changelog_entry: observability: Add token-quality signals (entropy, repetition, alignment) and entropy-segmentation cohorts; dashboards and default alert rule added. Feature-flag gated.
additional_context: Design doc: docs/obs/token-quality.md. Microbenchmarks attached in commit messages. This PR intentionally keeps token payloads truncated and never emits raw token text to logs for privacy; only compact anchors and token-level scores are exposed.
examples_of_use:
1) To enable for a tenant: toggle observability.token_quality=true in tenant config.
2) Query: sum(token_repetition_score) by (route, entropy_segment) over 1h.
3) To triage alert: open token-quality-degrade alert -> click trace anchor -> retrieve compact log shard via trace-anchors API.
notes: Follow-on tasks created: ENG-4300 (language-specific thresholds), ENG-4301 (eval integration), ENG-4302 (enterprise Dedicated policy).
